problem: Outdoor navigation stacks plan only within a local metric map or fixed-horizon policy, and treat unknown space beyond it as fixed cost. This produces myopic decisions that lead robots into dead ends or difficult terrain such as tree lines and walls.
motivation: Long-range off-road navigation without prior maps needs less myopic decisions, but building large metric maps is intractable because depth is sparse and noisy. Human operators can pick a long-range strategy from the camera feed alone, for example by spotting an opening in a tree line, which suggests that identifying good frontier directions is enough.
key_idea: Learn a goal-agnostic image-space 'affordable frontier' heatmap from camera images, trained on automatically labeled ego-centric videos. Project it to angular headings, weight by goal direction, and feed the best heading as a subgoal to the local planner.
insight: Affordance-based frontier selection from a frozen SAM/MobileSAM encoder gives earlier avoidance of obstacles than the goal heuristic, and needs no depth or map. The threshold ablation (Dump course, 5 trials per threshold) shows a U-shaped effect: too low a threshold makes everything affordable and the robot behaves like the Goal Heuristic, too high leaves almost nothing affordable. The best value was 0.7, and the slope of distance versus threshold from 0 to 0.7 was significant (p<0.05). Offline, human-labeled affordances beat auto-labeled ones on most metrics, so label quality limits performance.
method: Affordance Backbone: a frozen SAM2 (Racer Heavy) or MobileSAM (Spot) image encoder plus a small 5-layer deconvolution decoder predicts a goal-agnostic affordable-frontier heatmap. It is trained with MSE loss and L2 regularization.

Automatic labeling from video: CoTracker tracks a grid of points through ego-centric walking videos run in reverse. The point where it becomes occluded marks the hotspot (1), the path leading up to it is 0, and the vertical column around the hotspot is also 0 to cut sky false positives. The rest of the image is unlabeled and incurs no loss. Videos are chopped into 2-minute segments.

Heatmap-to-heading projection: heatmap scores are projected via camera intrinsics into 5° angular bins and summed per bin. Bins below h_thresh are zeroed, overlapping cameras are combined by max, scores are normalized, and an EMA (α=0.1) smooths them over time.

Goal-conditioned head: the filtered bin scores are multiplied by a Gaussian around the goal heading (σ_g) and a Gaussian around the previous selected heading (σ_p) for consistency. The argmax bin becomes the frontier heading. Near the goal, Spot reduces σ_g linearly within 30 m and heads straight to the goal within 12 m.

Integration with the local stack: the selected heading is placed as a goal at the edge of the local costmap (just outside its range for Spot), replacing the true goal for the existing planner. Spot uses an elevation map, ARA* and Spot's internal locomotion, and Racer Heavy uses its 50 m costmap planner. On Spot, LRN runs at ~4 Hz on a Jetson Orin AGX with front and rear fisheye cameras.
Human-labeled variant: for Racer Heavy, 1,901 human-labeled images (augmented to 11,406) train the same backbone, with Gaussian blur around positive labels.

setting.backbone: SAM2 (Racer Heavy) / MobileSAM (Spot) frozen encoder + small trained deconvolution decoder; hand-tuned goal-conditioned head
setting.model_size: 5-layer decoder on frozen SAM2/MobileSAM encoder; MobileSAM runs ~4 Hz on Jetson Orin AGX
setting.training_data: Spot: 54 min of Insta360 ego-centric human walking video from two semi-urban sites, auto-labeled via CoTracker into 92,711 heatmap labels. Racer Heavy: 1,901 human-labeled front-camera images from a California oak savanna, augmented to 11,406.
setting.observation: Monocular RGB fisheye (front+rear Insta360 on Spot; 3 front + 1 rear cameras on Racer Heavy), plus GPS goal heading; the local stack uses lidar/depth costmaps
setting.action_space: Heading (5° angular bin) chosen as subgoal for a local planner, which outputs velocity/path tracking
setting.privileged: none (GPS localization and goal waypoint given)

results: On Spot, LRN had zero human interventions on all three courses, while every baseline (Goal Heuristic, Traversability+Depth Anything V2, NoMaD) incurred some. It beat the Goal Heuristic on all metrics on Dump and Night and was comparable on Helipad. On the Racer Heavy 660 m run (single trial), LRN needed 0 interventions versus 1 for the Goal Heuristic, with higher average speed (4.98 vs 4.02 m/s) but a longer path (1435 vs 942 m). Offline, LRN outperforms Traversability+Depth Anything V2 on all metrics.
limitations: No explicit depth: angular distance to the goal is used as a proxy, so multiple hotspots at similar angles cause wandering and switching between directions.

Auto-labeled affordances are noisy (tracking errors), making the Spot model over-optimistic, and the method has no memory for backtracking from dead ends. It is a heuristic with no guarantee of improvement.

Small-scale evaluation: 5 trials per course on Spot and only one trial on Racer Heavy, with the Racer Heavy result using an earlier human-labeled version. Generalization is mainly to scenes near the training distribution.
